questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in an English-speaking country that was not too far away from home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I think studying abroad was a really great experience. However, due to exams during the winter, I arrived two weeks into the semester, which meant that I missed the introduction/orientation week. As a result, it was a bit more difficult to meet new people in the beginning.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. They have a website with all the necessary information, but it can be a bit difficult to navigate because there is so much information available.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: One person helped me carry my bags to the apartment, but apart from that, nothing else.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were many accommodation options on campus at different price levels. I stayed in the cheapest option, where four people share an apartment with two bathrooms and a kitchen, while each person has their own private bedroom. This arrangement was perfectly fine.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a store on campus called Centra. It has the basic essentials you need, but not much more. Otherwise, you can walk about 20 minutes to a larger supermarket. There are also plenty of cafés and coffee shops on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is definitely easiest to live on campus because you spend a lot of time at the university, and the campus functions like a small town in itself, with restaurants, cafés, a cinema, a swimming pool, and several different fitness centers. There are also several bus routes that take you into the city center, and the journey usually takes around 30 minutes. It is important to buy a student bus pass, as this makes public transportation significantly cheaper.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It is definitely easiest to live on campus because you spend a lot of time at the university, and the campus functions like a small town in itself, with restaurants, cafés, a cinema, a swimming pool, and several different fitness centers. There are also several bus routes that take you into the city center, and the journey usually takes around 30 minutes. It is important to buy a student bus pass, as this makes public transportation significantly cheaper.

It always felt very safe and peaceful living on campus. Security staff regularly patrolled the area in the evenings, and cleaning services maintained the apartment buildings and outdoor areas several times a week.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to register for courses, and students also had the opportunity to change their courses during the semester if they were not satisfied with their initial choices.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I do not remember the process exactly, but I believe I received a link where I could fill in the necessary information. Otherwise, I contacted the module coordinator to ask if I could be enrolled in the course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to enroll in all the modules I wanted to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend looking into the different modules in advance, paying particular attention to the assessment methods used throughout the semester and the style of teaching for each course. This can help ensure that the modules match your interests and preferred way of learning.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied overall. However, some courses required a fairly large workload and a significant amount of independent study. The lab sessions were relatively simple and manageable compared to those in Denmark.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I studied abroad during my 6th semester, which in Denmark corresponds to the final semester of a bachelor's degree. However, in Ireland, bachelor's degrees typically last four years. As a result, we were able to take courses from both the third and fourth years of the Irish bachelor's program.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same as in Copenhagen

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: PHAR30030 - Toxicology, PHAR40050 - Drug Discovery & Development, BIOC40220 - Hot topics in Biochemistry and BMOL40330 - Biomol. Sci. Research Project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I recommed Hot topics, there are very few contact hours, and there is no required reading material to go through. Overall, we had to complete one presentation and three assignments, all based on a scientific article that we selected ourselves. The lecturer is very friendly and supportive, and the module is very popular among students.
Then i would recommend Drug discovery, i believe there were around 12 lectures in total. They were very interesting, and the lecturers were highly knowledgeable and engaging. The module is assessed through a final exam at the end of the semester, which determines your entire grade. The exam consists of an essay-style assignment in which you are required to answer two questions.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In general, Dublin is an expensive city to live in. The supermarket on campus was quite expensive, laundry facilities were costly, and eating out was particularly expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee is cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: On campus, there are countless opportunities to stay active, including fitness centers, running clubs and activities, swimming pools, and yoga classes.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can sign up for the campus gym, which offers a wide range of facilities, equipment, and fitness activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ResLife app offered a wide variety of activities that students could sign up for, including cooking classes, board game nights, painting and drawing sessions, video game events, and coffee crawls. It was a great way to meet new people and get involved in campus life.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: At the beginning of the semester, students have the opportunity to sign up for a variety of organized trips around Ireland. Some are day trips, while others last several days. These trips tend to sell out very quickly, so it is important to book early. I personally visited Kilkenny and Galway, and both were great experiences.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. In general, Irish people are some of the friendliest and most welcoming people you will meet, so do not hesitate to ask for help if you need it. They are usually very happy to assist.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There is a bar on campus, which is a great place to meet new people and socialize with other students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendliness and pride in being Irish were very inspiring.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be a little challenging and overwhelming at first, and it is easy to become stressed. However, it is important to remember to enjoy your new surroundings and appreciate the opportunity to study abroad. Make the most of your time there by exploring as much as possible, trying new experiences, and taking advantage of everything the exchange experience has to offer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I completed my bachelor's project there, and it was more demanding than I had initially expected. The lab environment was quite different from what I was used to in Denmark, and we worked with a number of techniques that I was unfamiliar with at the beginning. However, I had an excellent supervisor who was very kind, supportive, and patient with me throughout the project.

If you choose to do your bachelor's project there, you should expect to spend time in the lab almost every day. While it can be challenging, it is also a great opportunity to gain hands-on experience and learn new laboratory techniques.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a new place that eventually came to feel like home was one of the most rewarding parts of the experience. It also gave me valuable insight into what studying is like in another part of the world. Most importantly, I had the opportunity to meet many new people, often with backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences very different from my own, which made the exchange experience even more enriching.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At times, there was a lot of work to manage, particularly because of the bachelor's project, which was very demanding and took up a significant amount of my time. As a result, it was easy to feel a bit stressed occasionally. However, with good planning and time management, it was possible to balance the workload while still enjoying the exchange experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: To summarize, I would recommend living on campus, choosing a few modules with a lighter workload, and arriving before the orientation week begins. Living on campus makes it much easier to meet people and take part in student life, while arriving in time for orientation gives you the best possible start to your exchange experience. It is also worth balancing your course choices so that you have enough time to enjoy everything the experience and Ireland have to offer.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
